locator.text: Display 101.2, p. 101, in the statement of Proposition 9.6

evidence: paper: C_m = \frac{\mathrm{i}\,n_\Phi \times t_m}{km|n_\Phi|^2}, \qquad \operatorname{curl}_*\!\left(C_m e^{ikm\Phi}\right) = (t_m + r_m)e^{ikm\Phi}, \qquad a_m = t_m + r_m.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The rewriting is purely notational, in three steps. (i) The Lean carries one real frequency parameter K where the paper writes the product km: phaseFactor K = K·i and carrier K Φ x = exp(K i Φ x), so carrier K Φ is the paper's e^{ikmΦ} exactly when K = km (HarmonicCalculus.lean:68,77). (ii) The amplitude of the Lean potential is inverseCarrier K • coefficient = (i/K) • (‖n_Φ‖²)⁻¹ • (n_Φ × t), which is the paper's C_m = i n_Φ × t_m /(km|n_Φ|²) term for term: same i, same cross product in the same order, same |n_Φ|² in the denominator, same single power of the frequency. NavierStokes.ActualCurrentParticularBounds.strippedPotential is that same expression as one definition body at the level of the actual construction. (iii) The Lean's realizedCoefficient a x + curlRemainder … is the paper's a_m = t_m + r_m, and it makes explicit what the paper leaves as prose ("r_m is the curl correction"): r_m = curl_* C_m, with no extra 1/km. In the Lean, curlRemainder is applied to `coefficient`, not to C_m: realizedCoefficient … x = a x + curlRemainder K … (coefficient …) x (CurlClassBounds.lean:603-605) and curlRemainder K … B x = (1/K) • (I • cylindricalCurl … B x) (CurlClassBounds.lean:269-271, restated as inverseCarrier K • cylindricalCurl … at :592-594); since by (ii) C_m = inverseCarrier K • coefficient = (i/K) • coefficient, curlRemainder K (coefficient) = (i/K) curl(coefficient) = curl((i/K) coefficient) = curl_* C_m. That is also what the paper forces: expanding curl_*(C_m e^{ikmΦ}) = (curl_* C_m + ikm n_Φ × C_m) e^{ikmΦ} and using ikm n_Φ × C_m = t_m (which is n_Φ × (n_Φ × t) = −|n_Φ|² t for n_Φ · t = 0, the content of normalCross_normalCoefficient, CurlClassBounds.lean:169-174) leaves exactly r_m = curl_* C_m, consistent with the paper's one-derivative gain r_m ∈ W_{α+1/2−κ_s} for t_m ∈ W_α. The Lean statement carries hypotheses the paper's display leaves implicit — K ≠ 0 (paper: m ∈ Z\{0}), n_Φ ≠ 0 on U, smoothness of Φ and of the amplitude, and the transversality normalDot n_Φ (a x) = 0 (paper: "For a transverse amplitude t_m", n_Φ · t_m = 0 in the notation table). Also, the paper's curl_* acts on the full harmonic C_m e^{ikmΦ} whereas the Lean states the identity for cylindricalCurl applied to vectorPotential, which is by definition that same harmonic.
